finding: The state-derived sidecar still referenced the mutable global STATUS.json. A watcher update after sidecar generation would change that canonical path's bytes and invalidate the pinned reference, so the same reconciliation could not be reproduced from a later checkout.
selected_design: Freeze the live state and matching aggregate status together before sidecar generation. Retain their original bytes at two write-once archive paths and require both hashes thereafter.
rejected_alternatives: Continue binding the global STATUS.json and regenerate the sidecar after each watcher update: this is mutable and races plan review.
Derive aggregate counts only from state.json and drop STATUS evidence: this loses the independent observer cross-check.
Copy state and status manually in separate commands: this cannot prove they describe one coherent observation.
implemented_guards: double-read both live files and reject any byte change within the capture window
require exact r9 run ID, plan digest, indices and task IDs
derive per-state counts from the harness task map and require equality to the aggregate observer snapshot
write the original byte sequences exactly once and refuse existing outputs
remove a partially published pair after an ordinary publication error
bind reconciliation and later window compilation only to the immutable archive paths

behaviors: freeze stable coherent source bytes and remain unchanged after the live source mutates
reject mismatched state/status counts without leaving output files

remaining_preconditions: population-gpu-current-r9 must reach a safe observed boundary
Local must run the current 290-method software-acceptance suite on the delivered source
Local must execute the canonical snapshot builder against the exact live r9 state and a matching refreshed STATUS.json
the resulting immutable pair and reconciliation sidecar must be returned and read back before window compilation
